cells.Requirement: The system shall refuse to proceed when a leftover staging area from an earlier run exists, aborting the run with a clear error that names it rather than proceeding into it. The refusal shall be CONDITIONED on evidence rather than on mere existence: a staging area that holds any file or subdirectory beyond its own owner record (hidden, system and dot-named entries included), that holds prune's ownership marker of any age, that is itself a link, or whose owner cannot be PROVED dead -- including any enumeration, stat, read or access failure, which classifies as indeterminate -- shall remain a refusal. A partial index left behind by a killed index write is not such an entry -- it is an incomplete copy of a file that still exists elsewhere, never the only copy of anything -- so it is ignored by exact, case-sensitive name and removed by exact name when the staging area is reclaimed or discarded (SR-083); every other entry still refuses. A staging area proved to hold neither content nor a live owner -- empty and itself stale, or carrying only an owner record that is stale by its own threshold and confirmed unchanged by a second sample (SR-075) -- shall instead be RECLAIMED non-destructively: moved aside under a unique name and the run continued. Nothing shall be deleted that has not first been moved aside, and any delete failure shall keep the aside folder. A run that aborts on this guard shall write no change folder and shall leave the tree byte-identical. The guard shall be entered ONLY when the staging area actually exists: a failure to create it for any other cause (no space, permission denied, path length) shall be logged verbatim and reported as itself, never as a leftover staging area.
cells.Rationale: Realizes SN-013; a leftover staging area means a prior run died mid-flight, and proceeding into a half-written one would mix two runs' evictions. An existence-only guard wedges the set after any external kill -- SIGKILL, OOM, container stop, power loss -- with every later scheduled run failing within about a second, silently, because nothing on disk distinguishes a dead owner from a live one; an interrupted run should not be a permanent interrupt. Refusal stays the DEFAULT because the opposite failure is real: removing a leftover staging area by hand can destroy the only physical copy of bytes a snapshot still needs, after which every restore of that snapshot fails as content missing. The guard therefore refuses on evidence instead of on ignorance. A create failure for any other cause is reported as itself so the real cause is never hidden behind a false 'staging area exists' message.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: Scoped to the externally interrupted BACKUP run; a killed prune is outside this criterion. REFUSAL: with a staging area holding a data file (hidden, system or dot-named included), prune's ownership marker, a fresh owner record, an owner record whose timestamp moves during the confirmation sample, an unreadable owner record, an enumeration error, an empty staging area whose own timestamp is fresh, or a staging area that is a symlink or junction, the run aborts naming it, writes no change folder, moves and deletes nothing, and every byte -- the run-state record included -- is hash-identical before and after. RECLAIM: with a staging area that is empty with a stale timestamp, or that holds only an owner record older than its own declared staleness threshold (reader floor 1800 s) AND unchanged in a confirmation sample about 90 s later, the run moves it aside under a unique name, logs [SR-075/reclaimed], and completes normally; the aside folder is removed only when it holds nothing but that owner record, and if anything else is present or a delete fails the folder is kept and the documented recovery is printed.

cells.Requirement: Snapshot removal shall run as an ordered transaction whose invariant is that the pool goes redundant before the snapshot disappears, never deficient: (0) a preflight with no mutation -- rails, indexes, witnesses, plan, capacity and orphan checks -- which is also exactly what -WhatIf reports; (1) each re-homed file copied on the same volume, verified, and published atomically; (2) every touched destination index published with its re-stamped witness; (3) a proof that, with the target excluded, EVERY surviving index entry still resolves -- a non-blank DataPath to a file present in its own folder whose form agrees with its Compressed column, a blank DataPath to a key present in the pool, whose located copies must additionally agree in form only when the entry's OWN folder carries a restore kit older than revision 2 (a revision-2+ kit decides a hash-recovered file's form from the located FILE, SR-050, so a form difference restores correctly and shall not block retention) -- aborting with the snapshot intact on any failure; (4) a commit that removes the snapshot from the view of every consumer (both restorers and the cross-change dedupe) in one atomic step, and only then its deletion. The operation shall refuse before mutating anything, each refusal reporting its SR-040 code with batch precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1: an index whose witness mismatches or is unparseable (3); an index with NO witness (3) unless the caller explicitly accepts an unverified index, the deliberate inverse of the restore default because restoring against an unverified index is recoverable and deleting against one is not; the SR-035 run-state gate (2); an existing staging area (2), which prune itself holds for its duration with its own ownership marker so a concurrent backup stops on the existing SR-017 guard; a target that is not an existing dated snapshot folder directly under the resolved change root, or any wildcard (2); data files in the target that its own index does not reference (2) unless the caller explicitly chooses to discard them; a pool that already fails to resolve, or whose located form disagrees with an entry's Compressed where that entry's folder carries a pre-revision-2 kit (2, naming the entries and the -RefreshKits remedy); insufficient free space at a destination volume (2), measured per destination volume with SR-052's volume identity and free-space measurement so the rail also exists on UNC and POSIX-rooted stores, and skipped rather than refused when a volume cannot be measured; a compressed plan with no usable archive tool (2); and a host I/O failure while copying (4, always before the commit point). A refusal shall mutate NOTHING; the single exception, deliberately scoped, is that before the named snapshot is planned the mechanism completes an outstanding deletion of that same snapshot that is already past the commit point and invisible to every consumer (residue for any other name is left alone). Recovery shall need no journal: re-running the same command recomputes the plan from disk, that name-scoped completion finishes an interrupted commit, and an entry sweep INSIDE the transaction -- after the rails pass and the staging area is held, so its failures classify as the retriable 4 -- removes the staged copies left behind, so an interruption at any phase boundary loses nothing. cells.Requirement: A stored data object shall be named "<hash>_<len><ext>", where <hash> is the row's complete 128-bit xxH2Hash encoded base-57 and left-padded to exactly 22 characters, <len> is the row's Length encoded base-57 with NO padding, '_' is the separator, and <ext> is the extension defined by SR-070. The base-57 alphabet shall be the 62 alphanumerics less the visually ambiguous 0, O, I, l and 1, and its first glyph ('2') shall be the zero digit. The encoder shall refuse, rather than truncate, a value too wide for a fixed-width field; the decoder shall refuse a field decoding to 2^128 or more; and a name shall be interpreted by taking the first 22 characters as the hash field and treating the extension as opaque.

The full hash is encoded because a truncated one cannot be compared with its index row by any audit. Base-57 dissolves the hostile-name classes rather than guarding against them and costs nothing: 57, 58 and 62 all encode 128 bits in 22 characters. An unpadded length avoids a visible run of zero digits. On a case-INSENSITIVE volume the 57 glyphs fold to 34 classes, so a name is worth 111.92 bits there rather than 128 - still well above the 94.12 bits of the earlier base-85 grammar.

cells.Rationale: Including hidden entries in every enumeration (SR-057) makes these two folders visible, and both then misbehave. On the restore side the same folder would count as a pool read failure and MISCLASSIFY the outcome: a row whose bytes are genuinely gone would be reported as StorageUnreadable / exit 4 ('fix this host and retry') rather than ContentMissing / exit 1, so an SR-040 wrapper would retry forever instead of reporting data loss. The volume-root condition is what confines the exclusion to folders that are the VOLUME's rather than the user's.

cells.Requirement: At the moment a backup run takes the staging area -- immediately after creating it, never before, or the write itself becomes the race -- the system shall record ownership of the staging area in an owner record inside it, placed and named to mirror prune's ownership marker so both holders are legible to one reader. The record shall carry a fresh run identity per acquisition, which every later ownership check compares against, together with diagnostic identity (set, host, container, boot, process), the start time, the heartbeat interval and the staleness threshold it commits to. It shall be written ONCE, never rewritten, and published by EXCLUSIVE CREATION: if an owner record already exists at publish time, this run has provably lost the staging area to a reclaimer that took it inside the create-to-record window, and it shall abort immediately, touching nothing, logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. A partially written record is read as torn with a FRESH timestamp, which classifies as a live owner and refuses -- the safe direction. LIVENESS shall be carried by the record's modification time, never by a process id: the writer may be a container sharing neither process namespace nor host with the reader, and the store may be exFAT. A heartbeat shall refresh the record for the whole life of the ownership, independently of whatever the run is busy with; each refresh shall be guarded by identity so that no late or queued refresh can freshen a successor's record; the FIRST refresh shall be performed at start and its effect VERIFIED, the run failing loudly when it does not land (a store that accepts the write but rejects the time change would otherwise make a live run classify dead after the threshold); a refresh that fails later shall be reported when the heartbeat stops; and stopping the heartbeat shall be idempotent and complete, so no refresh can land after ownership ends, on every exit path. An owner shall be judged DEAD if and only if the record's modification time is older than the staleness threshold the RECORD committed to, subject to a reader floor of 1800 s that a future schema may lengthen but never shorten, AND a second sample taken at least one heartbeat interval plus margin later -- never less than 90 s, and bounded so a hostile or corrupt record cannot stall the reclaim indefinitely -- shows it UNCHANGED. A record that does not parse supplies no interval and gets the 90 s floor. The confirmation sample is clock-free and is what makes the age test safe. A future-dated time shall be treated as fresh. CLASSIFICATION shall be decidable from the disk alone and fail-closed: hidden and system entries are content like any other, an enumeration, stat or access FAILURE is never evidence of emptiness and refuses as indeterminate, and a staging area that is a link is refused outright, since moving or deleting through one acts on a tree this guard never classified. The verdicts shall be: empty with a STALE timestamp, reclaim; empty with a FRESH timestamp, refuse, because a live run may be inside its own create-to-record window; owner record only, stale by age and confirmed, reclaim; owner record only, fresh or moving during the confirmation sample, refuse and say truthfully that a run is active; an owner record that cannot be PARSED (torn, truncated or an unknown schema) is judged by its modification time alone with the 1800 s floor and is never an error, a torn record being precisely the signature of a writer that died mid-publish; an owner record that cannot be READ refuses, absence of evidence not being evidence of death; prune's ownership marker of any age refuses (SR-046 mutual exclusion); any other file or subdirectory refuses. RECLAIM shall be a MOVE aside, never a delete in place, and no delete within it shall be recursive: the staging area is classified (taking the confirmation sample on the stale branches) and moved aside under a unique name, refusing on any failure without retrying in a loop; the moved folder is re-checked against the identity the classification saw and, on any mismatch, moved straight back and the run refused (keeping it and refusing loudly if the move back fails), because a move is bound to a path, not to the directory that was classified; the run then recreates the staging area and immediately publishes its own owner record, refusing on either failure and leaving the aside folder in place; finally the aside folder is re-examined and deleted only if it still holds nothing but the old record (or nothing at all), anything else or any I/O doubt keeping it, logging loudly and printing the documented recovery, and a failed delete keeping the folder and letting the run continue. Every cleanup of the staging area after an early failure shall PROVE ownership before deleting anything -- this run's owner record present, and nothing in the folder beyond it and this run's own staged copies of files that still exist in the backup root -- and shall then delete only those exact files, the record last, keeping the folder and logging [SR-075/lock-lost] on any mismatch, foreign content or I/O doubt, and reporting the original failure either way. Because a plain filesystem offers no true lease, the run shall FENCE the residual two-writer window by re-checking its ownership immediately before each phase that mutates the staging area, the pool or the authoritative index -- the staged index write, the eviction of removed files, the preservation of superseded data, the backup-root index publish with its witness, and the finalization into a dated snapshot -- and on a mismatch abort immediately and CLEAN UP NOTHING, the folder no longer being this run's to delete, logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. An UNREADABLE record at a fence shall be retried briefly before it is treated as lost, while an identity MISMATCH aborts on the first read, so one network blip cannot strand a content-holding staging area. The owner record shall be removed -- heartbeat stopped first -- immediately before the staging area becomes a dated snapshot, so no owner record ever reaches a snapshot, where prune's unreferenced-data rail (SR-046) would refuse it. Each branch shall emit a distinct, greppable token into the set log: [SR-075/reclaimed], [SR-075/owner-live], [SR-075/content-refused], [SR-075/prune-held], [SR-075/lock-lost], and [SR-075/lock-held]. No new exit code shall be introduced. The window from the owner record's removal to the staging area becoming a snapshot carries NO record, NO heartbeat and NO fence, so nothing in this requirement can show that a run there is alive; that window shall be covered instead by the staging OS lock (SR-085), which every backup takes BEFORE it creates or classifies the staging area and releases only after that step has completed (or on any failure), and which prune takes too. Two rules bind every reader of it: a lock that cannot be opened for ANY reason is a LIVE holder, and the caller refuses touching nothing; and a lock this run acquired is NOT evidence that a staging area's owner is dead -- an older FileBackup takes no OS lock -- so every classification and reclaim rule above still decides exactly as before, the lock only ever adding a refusal (SR-086). The owner record, heartbeat, fences and confirmation sample all remain.
cells.Rationale: A staging lock that is a bare directory, released only on handled failures, is held forever by a run killed from outside -- the SR-017 wedge. Prune already records its ownership in a marker, so giving the backup's lock an owner record makes both lock-holders legible to the same reader. Each element exists because a cheaper version of it is unsafe. A process id is meaningless across a container boundary on an exFAT store, so the modification time carries liveness. A single non-exclusive write can be torn by a process that dies mid-write, and the create-to-record window lets a reclaimer steal a LIVE lock, so the publish is exclusive and the victim aborts, and a staging area with no record is reclaimable only when the directory itself is stale. A computed age compares two clocks, and the DANGEROUS direction is the writer being behind -- which would make a live, continuously beating owner look instantly stale to a fast reader -- so a clock-free confirmation sample decides instead, and it absorbs remote-volume metadata caching for free. A heartbeat that cannot fire while the run is busy (hashing a 100 GB file, say), or that dies silently, makes a silently dead beat indistinguishable from a healthy one, so the beat must run independently of the run's work and its failure must be visible. A late refresh could freshen a successor's record, so refreshes are identity-guarded and stopping waits them out. Re-enumerating and then deleting recursively still leaves a window in which a just-arrived data file is swept up, so the deletes are named files plus a non-recursive directory delete that the filesystem itself fails when anything unexpected is present -- the move-aside is the documented safe recovery action, and the final re-examination is the design's safety proof rather than belt and braces. The threshold asymmetry is total -- too long costs a slower automatic recovery, too short costs stomping a live run -- so 1800 s is a 30x margin over the heartbeat and is deliberately not exposed as a setting. What remains, a process frozen past the threshold resurrecting mid-phase, is accepted because the alternative is strictly worse: that same frozen run racing a human performing the manual move-aside, with no record, no fence and no detection at all. The branch tokens exist because the observed failure was a one-second clean-looking abort that no wrapper could alarm on; IF-001 stays a fixed contract and the backup host keeps alarm policy, so facts go into the log and exit codes are not renumbered.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: A run killed from outside leaves a staging area holding only its owner record; a later run started more than the record's staleness threshold afterwards takes the confirmation sample, moves the folder aside under a unique name, logs [SR-075/reclaimed], completes with exit 0, and the aside folder is gone. While the first run is ALIVE the second refuses with [SR-075/owner-live] and a message naming the owning host and process, the time it started and the seconds since its last heartbeat, and the tree is byte-identical before and after. The heartbeat advances the record's modification time, observed from a SEPARATE process, WHILE a long blocking hash occupies the run, and a heartbeat made to fail neither kills the run nor stops the beat unnoticed. A staging area holding a stale record PLUS a data file, prune's ownership marker, an unreadable record, hidden or system entries, an enumeration error, or a staging area that is a symlink each refuse with the matching token, move and delete nothing, and leave every file hash-identical. A torn or unknown-schema record falls back to its modification time with the 1800 s floor and still reclaims when stale. Two reclaimers racing one stale lock leave exactly one staging area, carrying the winner's run identity, the loser refusing. A victim paused between creating the staging area and publishing its record, whose staging area is reclaimed meanwhile, fails its exclusive publish and aborts touching nothing, logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. Data files appearing in the folder between classification and move, or in the aside folder between the final re-examination and the delete, each leave the aside folder KEPT with its bytes intact and the recovery text printed. A record swapped for a different run identity at each fence point aborts the run before that phase mutates the pool and cleans up nothing. A writer clock set behind the reader beyond the threshold, with the owner alive and beating, still refuses. No owner record appears in any produced dated snapshot, on the changed, no-op or first-run path, and such a snapshot prunes without an unreferenced-data refusal. The reclaim is demonstrated end to end on a real exFAT volume under Windows and inside the container on the deployment's Linux-over-exFAT stack.

cells.Requirement: When CompressEnabled is true the system shall decide the stored form of a NEWLY WRITTEN object from the BYTES rather than from the filename, by a sampled compressibility probe composed AFTER the SR-004 extension list. The decision shall depend only on CompressEnabled, the CompressProbe mode, the extension list's answer, the file's length, the probe floor and the probe's measurement, and shall carry one Reason in {CompressDisabled, ModeOff, BelowFloor, ListExempt, ProbeUnavailable, ProbeCompressible, ProbeIncompressible}, evaluated IN THIS ORDER: (0) CompressEnabled=false -> raw, CompressDisabled, and NOTHING BELOW RUNS - no probe is taken, the archive tool is not needed, and a Plain set can never name an object .7z nor record Compressed=Yes; (2) mode off -> the list's answer; (3) length below the floor -> the list's answer, BelowFloor; (4) mode excluded-extensions and the list says no -> raw, ListExempt; (5) the probe returned no measurement -> THE LIST'S ANSWER, ProbeUnavailable, with one WARN; (6) compressed sample bytes <= (1 - threshold) x sampled bytes -> compress, ProbeCompressible; (7) otherwise -> raw, ProbeIncompressible. No name-based override of the measurement exists in any mode, so an object whose name says already-compressed but whose bytes measure compressible is stored compressed, and the reverse. The threshold shall be 0.10 and shall be applied to the AGGREGATE of the sampled windows, never to any single window: a multi-gigabyte random file with a 64 KiB text head reads about 0.93 and stays raw, while a file one third of which is text reads about 0.7 and is compressed. The floor shall be 256 KiB: a file below it shall never be probed and shall take the list's answer in every mode. The probe shall open the source read-only, with the same sharing as the hasher and the stored-form check so that probe success predicts copy success; it shall never measure a file that changes while it is sampled - where the platform cannot exclude a writer, it shall compare the file's length and last-write time before and after sampling and yield NO measurement when either changed - and it shall sample three windows of 256 KiB at the start, middle and end of the file, each filled completely unless end-of-file is reached; when the file is shorter than three windows it shall instead read the whole file once as a single sample. A path that cannot be opened shall yield no measurement rather than an error. The probe shall be taken LAZILY and at most ONCE PER CONTENT GROUP: only when the group's content is about to be written, never for a prior-backup dedup hit and never for an in-run twin (nothing already stored is ever re-formed, SR-061), and never more than once per group even when one member's copy fails and a later member succeeds. It shall try the group's readable CANDIDATES - the owner and then every member, the same list the copy already tries, so a locked owner cannot fail a group a readable twin can serve - and sample the first that opens; only when NONE opens is the decision ProbeUnavailable. The probe shall never fail, slow or misdirect a run beyond its own read cost: every probe read failure shall be contained, at most 3 x 256 KiB shall be read per WRITTEN group, no probe read shall be attempted per file or per failed attempt, and the destination shall never be opened. The mode shall be carried by the optional per-set configuration key CompressProbe with the EXACT-LOWERCASE vocabulary off | excluded-extensions | always, defaulting to always, an absent key resolving to always (SR-042 / SR-063). Each written group's decision shall be logged ONCE at DEBUG as 'compress-decision: <rel> <Reason> ratio=<aggregate> windows=<r1,r2,r3>', and the per-set summary shall carry physical-object counters counted only after a successful write: 'Probe stored raw: <n> objects, <bytes>', 'Probe compressed: <n>' and 'Probe reads: <bytes>', the last being the first-run cost figure the operator is owed. Stated as explicit NON-CLAIMS: nothing already stored is re-formed in either direction and there is no migration (SR-061); no restorer is involved and no restore decision changes (SR-050, SR-068 - restore is insensitive to the Compressed column); NO new exit code is introduced and ConfigVersion stays 2, IF-001 gaining a note only; and the stored object name's extension and the row's Compressed column shall both continue to derive from the ONE decision, so the name cannot lie (SR-004).
cells.Rationale: An extension list decides from the filename alone, and on a real library it missed a genuine archive type: 649 genuine 7z archives, 880 GB, 43% of the data, re-compressed at the highest level for a measured 5% gain at roughly 20 minutes of two-core CPU per file - about nine days to save 47 GB. The archive format's own incompressible-chunk fallback prevents the SPACE penalty and never the TIME penalty, because it decides after the match-finder has run; only the caller can decide before. Cross-checking the list against a second list that shares the same blind spot does not help, so maintaining it harder is not the fix - the name is not evidence, and 768 KiB of the actual bytes is. SN-003's example file types are examples of the need, not rulings on those formats, so the measurement is never overridden by name. The rule is AGGREGATE rather than any-sample because an any-sample rule re-creates the original failure mode, sending a mostly-random file to the slowest compression because its head happened to be text. Rule 0 comes first because a rule that consulted the probe before CompressEnabled would name an archive object and record Compressed=Yes on a Plain set for which the archive tool is not even resolved, and the copy would raw-copy under that lying name. The list-answer fallback rather than a failure keeps the probe structurally incapable of costing a file: a lock costs a decision, never data, which is what keeps unattended runs unattended (SN-011). Laziness and one probe per group keep the added read proportional to WRITTEN groups rather than to files or to failed attempts - a probe taken per member would re-probe and re-WARN for every failing member. Threshold 0.10 and the 256 KiB floor are fixed values rather than configuration keys: they are two settings nobody can measure, while the MODE is the operator's lever. Determinism holds within a run and host - fixed offsets, fixed sample size, fixed codec and level - and the one known limit is stated rather than hidden: a ratio landing inside noise of the threshold could flip across runtime versions, which can only affect an object's FIRST write, and where both outcomes are correct storage forms that restore byte-exact.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: With CompressEnabled=false, every mode x every extension class (SN-003's example names, listed, unlisted, none) stores raw with Compressed=No and no probe is taken. Under the default mode always, above the 256 KiB floor: random bytes are stored raw; text is stored .7z; a random file with a 64 KiB text head is stored raw; a file one third text is stored .7z; a listed .zip over text is stored .7z and the same .zip over random is stored raw; a .docx over random bytes is stored RAW and a .jpg over text bytes is stored .7z; and in EVERY arm the stored object name's extension and the row's Compressed column agree. Under off the same inputs reproduce the list's answer exactly - .7z for the .docx, raw for the .jpg, .7z for a .txt. Under excluded-extensions a listed extension is still exempted while everything the list would compress is probed. Below the floor every mode takes the list's answer. A file smaller than three samples is read exactly ONCE as a single sample; a vanished path and a path held exclusively by another process each yield no measurement; a group in which no member can be opened yields the LIST'S answer plus exactly one WARN and the run still exits 0. Random bytes never measure below 0.98 aggregate. A prior-backup dedup hit and an in-run twin cause no probe at all; a group whose first member's copy fails and whose second succeeds probes EXACTLY once and warns at most once; a locked owner with a readable twin samples the twin and does not report ProbeUnavailable. One compress-decision line is emitted per written group at DEBUG, and the set summary reports Probe stored raw, Probe compressed and Probe reads. An unchanged v2 configuration loads and resolves CompressProbe to always; a mixed-case "Always", "maybe", a null and a number are each refused with status 2 naming the key, in JSON and in CLIXML alike, creating nothing. -Action Verify over a probe-mixed store reports clean, and both restorers reproduce every object byte-exact.

cells.Requirement: Every backup run, every prune, every storage-form repair (-RepairStorage) and every snapshot kit refresh (-RefreshKits) shall hold an exclusive, non-blocking operating-system lock on the staging lock file at the root of the change root -- outside the staging area -- for the whole of its mutation of the store; the repair and the refresh shall take it themselves, so a caller of the mechanism that bypasses the entry point is covered exactly like the entry point, and their -WhatIf forms, like a read-only -Action Verify, -Action Snapshots, -Action View (which writes only the view root outside both store roots) and every restore, shall take none. A backup shall take it BEFORE it reads any store state its decisions depend on -- the prior backup's completion time, the SR-035 run-state gate and the index-witness gate -- and therefore before it creates or classifies the staging area; only path resolution precedes it, and the set log is opened (truncated) only after it and after those gates, a refusal on the lock APPENDING one line to the set log because that log belongs to the live holder. It shall release it only after the staging area has become a dated snapshot, or on any failure, refusal or lost-ownership return; it is held until the set's work is finished, past the run-state write and the cross-change dedupe. The window from the owner record's removal to that step, in which no record, heartbeat or ownership fence exists, shall therefore always be covered by the lock. A prune shall take it before anything it does -- the completion of an already-committed removal included -- and hold it for the whole batch; -WhatIf, which mutates nothing, shall take none. A reclaim of an abandoned staging area (SR-017, SR-075) runs inside the backup that holds the lock. A process kill releases the lock, because the operating system closes the handle however the holder ends. PLATFORM GUARANTEE: on Windows the lock is a mandatory share mode that every opener honours, and over SMB the server enforces it among SMB clients. On Linux and macOS it is ADVISORY: it excludes every process that takes the same lock on the same file -- every FileBackup on the same kernel, FileBackup containers sharing a bind-mounted volume included -- but not a process that does not lock; it is silently absent (the open succeeds unlocked) when the filesystem does not support it or file locking is disabled in the runtime; and it is NOT guaranteed to exclude a process on another host reaching the same store through an SMB or NFS client, nor a Windows client reaching a Linux-hosted store through Samba, whose share modes and the server's local locks do not see each other. Where the lock does not exclude, the SR-075 owner record, heartbeat and confirmation sample remain the only protection.
cells.Rationale: Between the owner record's removal and the staging area becoming a snapshot nothing signals that a run is alive -- no record, no heartbeat, no fence -- while the staging area holds the only copy of evicted and superseded bytes. A killed run's staging must recover by itself, and that recovery has to tell a killed run from a live one in exactly that window. An OS lock is the one liveness signal a dead process cannot keep asserting. A run that reads store state before taking the lock can act on state another run has not yet written: with no prior completion time yet it takes itself for a first backup and deletes a staging area holding superseded bytes the other run has just moved. Repair and kit refresh rewrite pool objects, indexes and snapshot kits, so they need the lock as much as a backup does. Prune takes the same lock because otherwise the lock excludes only recovery: once the staging area is gone, the staging-area rail cannot see a backup that is still rewriting snapshot indexes in the cross-change dedupe. Holding it past that step costs nothing and closes that. Two FileBackup processes on one host against one store are a real case: a backup host that is killed mid-wrapper can leave the container running while a later wrapper starts another.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: On Windows: a run held at each end of the no-record window (just after the owner record's removal, and just before the staging area becomes a snapshot with the blanked index and kit in it) holds the lock, and a concurrent backup and a concurrent prune each refuse with [SR-075/lock-held] leaving every file under BackupPath and ChangePath unchanged; a prune against a backup held just after the staging area became a snapshot is Refused with code 2 and changes no byte; a backup against a prune held inside its transaction refuses on the lock and changes no byte; a storage-form repair over a genuinely repairable finding and a kit refresh over a genuinely stale snapshot kit, each against a backup held in the no-record window, are refused with [SR-075/lock-held] and change no byte (and do their work once the backup is gone), and through the entry point -Action Verify -RepairStorage and -RefreshKits exit 2 while a read-only -Action Verify still exits 0; the lock is free after a normal completion, an ordinary failure after staging began, an early refusal, a tripped ownership fence, and a forced kill of the holder. Not claimed here: any Linux, macOS or container run -- the advisory behaviour above is documented platform behaviour, not a measurement.
